points.title: 早期教育
points.description: 埃米·诺特出生于埃尔朗根的一个犹太数学家庭，父亲马克斯·诺特是著名的数学家。尽管当时女性接受高等教育面临诸多限制，诺特仍在家中接受了良好的教育，并展现出非凡的数学天赋。这一时期，她学习了语言、音乐和基础科学，为后来的数学研究奠定了基础。埃尔朗根的学术环境对她早期的学术兴趣产生了深远影响，尽管当时女性被禁止正式进入大学学习。
points.descriptionEn: Emmy Noether was born in Erlangen, Germany, into a Jewish family of mathematicians, with her father Max Noether being a prominent mathematician. Despite the restrictions on higher education for women at the time, Noether received excellent homeschooling and demonstrated extraordinary mathematical talent. During this period, she studied languages, music, and basic sciences, laying the foundation for her later mathematical research. Erlangen's academic environment profoundly influenced her early academic interests, although women were formally prohibited from attending university at that time.

points.title: 博士学位研究
points.description: 1900年，诺特获准作为旁听生进入埃尔朗根大学，这是当时德国少数允许女性入学的大学之一。1907年，她在保罗·戈尔丹的指导下获得博士学位，论文主题是关于不变量的研究。这一时期，诺特开始展现出在代数不变量理论方面的非凡才能，尽管她仍然无法获得正式的学术职位，只能以非正式身份继续研究工作。埃尔朗根大学的经历为她后来的学术生涯奠定了基础，尽管性别歧视仍然限制了她的职业发展。
points.descriptionEn: In 1900, Noether was permitted to enroll as an auditor at the University of Erlangen, one of the few German universities that allowed women at the time. In 1907, she earned her doctorate under the supervision of Paul Gordon, with her dissertation focusing on invariant theory. During this period, Noether began demonstrating exceptional talent in algebraic invariant theory, though she still could not obtain a formal academic position and could only continue her research informally. Her experience at Erlangen laid the foundation for her later academic career, despite gender discrimination still limiting her professional development.

points.title: 学术巅峰期
points.description: 1915年，诺特应大卫·希尔伯特和菲利克斯·克莱因的邀请前往哥廷根大学，尽管她最初只能以希尔伯特的名义授课。1919年，她终于获得了正式的教职，成为哥廷根大学历史上第一位女性教授。在哥廷根期间，诺特发展了她最重要的数学贡献，包括诺特定理（连接对称性与守恒定律）和诺特环理论。她吸引了来自世界各地的学生和研究者，形成了著名的'诺特学派'。这一时期，她的工作对抽象代数的发展产生了革命性影响，并深刻影响了爱因斯坦的广义相对论研究。
points.descriptionEn: In 1915, Noether was invited to the University of Göttingen by David Hilbert and Felix Klein, though she initially could only lecture in Hilbert's name. In 1919, she finally obtained a formal faculty position, becoming the first female professor in Göttingen's history. During her time in Göttingen, Noether developed her most important mathematical contributions, including Noether's Theorem (connecting symmetry and conservation laws) and Noetherian ring theory. She attracted students and researchers from around the world, forming the famous 'Noether school.' This period saw her work have a revolutionary impact on the development of abstract algebra and profoundly influenced Einstein's research on general relativity.

points.place: 美国宾夕法尼亚州布林莫尔学院
points.title: 流亡美国
points.description: 1933年，纳粹上台后，作为犹太人的诺特被剥夺了在哥廷根大学的职位。在阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦和其他国际学者的帮助下，她接受了美国布林莫尔学院的邀请前往美国。在布林莫尔，诺特继续她的数学研究，并在普林斯顿高等研究院担任客座教授。尽管面临语言障碍和适应新环境的挑战，诺特仍然活跃于数学界，指导学生并继续发表重要论文。1935年，她在一次手术后去世，年仅53岁。布林莫尔的经历虽然短暂，但诺特在这里完成了她最后的重要工作，并对美国数学界产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1933, after the Nazi rise to power, Noether, as a Jewish person, was stripped of her position at the University of Göttingen. With the help of international scholars including Albert Einstein, she accepted an invitation to Bryn Mawr College in the United States. At Bryn Mawr, Noether continued her mathematical research and also served as a visiting professor at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton. Despite facing challenges such as language barriers and adapting to a new environment, Noether remained active in the mathematical community, advising students and continuing to publish important papers. In 1935, she died at the age of 53 following surgery. Though her time at Bryn Mawr was brief, Noether completed her most important work there and had a profound impact on American mathematics.

points.place: 美国宾夕法尼亚州布林莫尔
points.title: 数学遗产
points.description: 诺特去世后，她的数学遗产继续影响着数学和物理学的发展。她的工作为现代代数几何、拓扑学和理论物理学奠定了基础。诺特定理已成为物理学中的基本原理，广泛应用于量子场论和粒子物理学。她的抽象代数方法改变了数学研究的方向，使数学家能够更深入地探索结构而非计算。20世纪后期，诺特被公认为历史上最伟大的数学家之一，她的名字被用于命名数学中的多个概念和定理。今天，'诺特环'、'诺特范畴'等概念已成为现代数学的标准术语，她的思想继续影响着新一代数学家。
points.descriptionEn: After Noether's death, her mathematical legacy continued to influence the development of mathematics and physics. Her work laid the foundation for modern algebraic geometry, topology, and theoretical physics. Noether's Theorem has become a fundamental principle in physics, widely applied in quantum field theory and particle physics. Her methods in abstract algebra transformed the direction of mathematical research, enabling mathematicians to explore structures rather than just computations. By the late 20th century, Noether was recognized as one of the greatest mathematicians in history, and her name has been given to numerous mathematical concepts and theorems. Today, terms like 'Noetherian rings' and 'Noetherian categories' are standard in modern mathematics, and her ideas continue to influence new generations of mathematicians.

supporter.zh: 埃米·诺特被广泛认为是历史上最杰出的数学家之一，她的抽象代数方法彻底改变了现代数学的面貌。支持者赞誉她为'抽象代数之母'，认为她开创性的工作为20世纪数学的发展奠定了基础。诺特定理作为连接对称性与守恒定律的基本原理，已成为现代物理学的基石。她突破性别障碍的勇气和对纯粹数学的执着追求，激励了无数后来的女性科学家和数学家。
supporter.en: Emmy Noether is widely regarded as one of the greatest mathematicians in history, and her abstract algebra methods revolutionized modern mathematics. Supporters hail her as the 'mother of abstract algebra,' believing her pioneering work laid the foundation for 20th-century mathematics. Noether's Theorem, as a fundamental principle connecting symmetry and conservation laws, has become a cornerstone of modern physics. Her courage in overcoming gender barriers and dedication to pure mathematics have inspired countless later female scientists and mathematicians.

critic.zh: 批评者指出诺特的工作过于抽象，脱离了数学的实际应用，认为她的理论过于形式化而缺乏直观性。一些数学家认为她过度强调结构而忽视了计算的重要性。此外，诺特在纳粹上台前未能充分认识到德国政治局势的严重性，直到被迫离开才意识到危险，这被一些人视为政治上的天真。还有人批评她在教学风格上过于专注自己的研究而忽视了对学生的直接指导。
critic.en: Critics point out that Noether's work was too abstract and disconnected from practical applications of mathematics, arguing that her theories were overly formalized and lacked intuition. Some mathematicians believe she overemphasized structures at the expense of computational importance. Additionally, critics note that Noether failed to fully recognize the severity of the German political situation before the Nazi rise to power, only realizing the danger when forced to leave, which some view as political naivety. Others criticize her teaching style for being too focused on her own research while neglecting direct guidance for students.

objective.zh: 从历史和流行文化视角看，埃米·诺特已成为女性在科学领域取得突破的象征。她的故事被广泛讲述，代表着在男性主导的学术世界中女性所面临的挑战与成就。在数学界，诺特被公认为抽象代数的奠基人，她的工作深刻影响了现代数学的发展轨迹。物理学界则将她视为理论物理学的关键人物，诺特定理已成为标准物理课程的重要组成部分。诺特的生平和成就已成为科学史上的经典案例，展示了个人才华如何克服社会障碍，最终改变科学发展的方向。
objective.en: From historical and popular culture perspectives, Emmy Noether has become a symbol of female breakthroughs in science. Her story is widely told, representing the challenges and achievements women faced in the male-dominated academic world. In mathematics, Noether is recognized as the founder of abstract algebra, and her work has profoundly influenced the trajectory of modern mathematics. In physics, she is regarded as a key figure in theoretical physics, with Noether's Theorem becoming an essential part of standard physics curricula. Noether's life and achievements have become a classic case study in the history of science, demonstrating how individual talent can overcome social barriers to ultimately change the direction of scientific development.

self.zh: 我并不明白为什么'性别'和'犹太人'这两个词会如此频繁地出现在我的名字前面。我只是一个数学家。
self.en: I do not see why 'sex' or 'Jewishness' should be stressed as characteristics that distinguish me. I am a mathematician.

others.zh: 根据当代数学家们的普遍意见，诺特小姐是自女性高等教育开始以来，最富有创造力的数学天才。
others.en: In the judgment of the most competent living mathematicians, Fräulein Noether was the most significant creative mathematical genius thus far produced since the higher education of women began.
